note: The 1952 Enchiridion controls the complete standalone boundary, all 31 substantive words and the eight-line punctuation. Key of Heaven 1901 supports every substantive word, including Vale at w023. Lasance 1906 instead prints Valde at w023; its resulting repetition, Valde, o valde decora, is recorded as a substantive lexical variant and not conflated with the selected recension. Both prayerbooks use coelorum, an orthographic accidental against the controlling caelorum. Capitalization, line punctuation and omitted vocative commas are typography or punctuation only. Seasonal rubrics, the following versicle, response, Oremus and collect are separate units and are excluded.

adjudicated.ruling: Cælórum follows the controlling Enchiridion's caelorum and the corpus orthography profile, which represents ae with the ligature and adds the customary stress accent. The prayerbooks' coelorum is the common oe spelling of the same word; their punctuation is recorded in the witness transcriptions.

recensional_comparators.ruling: Vale is the controlling 1952 reading and is independently supported by Key of Heaven 1901. It supplies the farewell imperative that answers the earlier greetings Ave and Salve. Lasance's Valde creates a repeated adverb, Valde, o valde decora; the complete alternate recension is preserved as a raw comparator and does not replace or silently merge with the selected recension.
